definition: Left heart border at its most lateral point (the left cardiac silhouette), as used for the cardiothoracic ratio.
Right heart border (right atrium) at its most lateral point, as used for the cardiothoracic ratio.
Inner margin of the {side} thoracic cage (lung edge against the ribs) at the level of the widest inner thoracic diameter above the diaphragm. Place the left and right points at the same rib level.

{Side} costophrenic angle: the lowest lateral corner of the aerated lung, where the hemidiaphragm meets the lateral chest wall. Use the visible lung, not the posterior recess seen through the diaphragm.
Point on the {side} lateral lung edge (chest wall), about 2 cm above the costophrenic angle. With the diaphragm point it defines the angle.
Point on the {side} hemidiaphragm contour, about 2 cm medial to the costophrenic angle.
{Side} cardiophrenic angle: where the {side} heart border meets the hemidiaphragm, on the aerated lung outline (on the right: where the right heart / IVC border meets the right hemidiaphragm).
Point on the {side} heart border, about 2 cm above the cardiophrenic angle.
Point on the {side} hemidiaphragm contour, about 2 cm lateral to the cardiophrenic angle.
Highest point of the {side} hemidiaphragm dome, lateral to the heart border.
Lateral edge of the {side} lung (pleural line) at the height of the hilum.
Apex of the {side} lung: the middle of its uppermost contour.
{Side} hilar point: where the upper-lobe pulmonary vein crosses the descending (lower-lobe) pulmonary artery, close to the mediastinum.
Right tracheobronchial angle: deepest point of the concave contour where the right tracheal wall turns into the right main bronchus (azygos region).
Right border of the upper mediastinum at the level of the aortic knob (for the mediastinal width).
Aortic knob: most lateral point of the aortic arch on the left mediastinal border.
Top of the aortic arch.
Aortopulmonary window: deepest (most medial) point of the left mediastinal contour between the aortic knob and the main pulmonary artery.
Pulmonary artery segment: most lateral point of the main pulmonary artery on the left mediastinal border, below the aortopulmonary window.
Carina: the tip of the tracheal bifurcation between the two main bronchi.
Midpoint of the {side} main bronchus, halfway along it from the carina.
Point on the inferior wall of the {side} main bronchus, about 2 cm from the carina (defines the subcarinal angle).
Centre of the trachea at the level of the medial clavicle ends.
Centre of the trachea in its upper part, about a quarter of its length below the top: upper point of the tracheal axis.
Centre of the trachea just above the carina: lower point of the tracheal axis.
Junction of the inferior vena cava with the right atrium (upper end of the IVC).
Gastro-oesophageal junction: lower end of the oesophagus where it enters the stomach. Usually inferred; mark unsure if it cannot be seen.
Highest point of the gastric fundus (gastric air bubble) under the left hemidiaphragm.
Cardiac apex: the infero-lateral tip of the heart above the left hemidiaphragm.
Cardiac waist: deepest (most medial) point of the left heart border between the pulmonary artery segment and the left ventricle.
Right edge of the left atrium seen through the heart (the double-density contour), where it is visible.
Left atrial appendage: point on the left heart border at the level of the left atrium, between the pulmonary artery segment and the left ventricle.
Jugular (suprasternal) notch: top of the manubrium in the midline.
Lateral end of the {side} clavicle at the acromioclavicular joint. Not visible if it lies outside the image.
Medial end of the {side} clavicle at the sternoclavicular joint (used for rotation).
Corner of the vertebral body: {side} end of the {part} endplate (patient's {side}). Mark the body itself, not the pedicles or transverse processes.
Anterior end of the bony rib, where it meets the costal cartilage. Count the ribs from the top.
Medial end of the posterior rib at the spine (rib head, costovertebral junction). Count the ribs from the top.
Point about 3 cm along the posterior rib from its head, on the rib's centre line. With the rib head it gives the slope of the rib.

definition: Centre of the {zone}: the centre of its area. The zones are horizontal bands of the lung; switch on the outlines (m) to see the band.
Minor (horizontal) fissure: the middle of the upper border of the right middle lobe.
Inferior angle (lowest tip) of the {side} scapula.
Point on the centre line of the {cls}, {pct} of its length from its upper end. Switch on the outlines (m) to see the vessel.
Centre of the {cls}: the centre of its area. Switch on the outlines (m) to see the organ.
Anterior costophrenic sulcus: where the diaphragm meets the anterior chest wall, below the aerated lung.
Posterior costophrenic sulcus: the deepest posterior point where the diaphragm meets the posterior chest wall (the first place pleural fluid collects).
Point on the {part} chest wall, about 2 cm above the {part} costophrenic sulcus.
Point on the diaphragm contour, about 2 cm from the {part} costophrenic sulcus.
Sternodiaphragmatic angle: where the anterior diaphragm meets the back of the lower sternum.
Point on the back of the sternum, about 2 cm above the sternodiaphragmatic angle.
Point on the diaphragm contour, about 2 cm behind the sternodiaphragmatic angle.
Highest point of the diaphragm contour.
Top of the lung apex (both apices overlap on the lateral view).
Back surface of the sternum about 3 cm below the manubriosternal junction: anterior border of the retrosternal clear space.
Anterior wall of the ascending aorta at the same height: posterior border of the retrosternal clear space.
Top of the aortic arch.
Most anterior point of the heart (behind the sternum).
Posterior heart border, about 2 cm above the point where the inferior vena cava meets the heart.
Antero-inferior tip of the heart, above the diaphragm.
Hoffman–Rigler point: the posterior heart border 2 cm above the intersection of the inferior vena cava and the heart (left ventricular enlargement if it lies more than 1.8 cm behind the IVC).
Jugular notch: the top of the manubrium.
Sternal angle: the junction of manubrium and sternal body.
Point on the centre line of the manubrium, about 2 cm above the sternal angle.
Point on the centre line of the sternal body, about 3 cm below the sternal angle.
Corner of the vertebral body: {part} end of the {part2} endplate. Mark the body itself, not the pedicles or the posterior elements.
